Castleford

Castleford will be hoping for another successful season under Daryl Powell. Since his appointment, Castleford have gone from strength to strength and it shows no sign of changing now. Powell has set an ambitious target of a top four finish this year, and if they are as consistent as the last few years they may achieve their targets. The main downside to the off-season was the loss of powerhouse winger Justin Carney to Salford on loan after an off the field incident. However, Castleford have recruited strongly in the backs. They have signed experienced winger Joeal Monaghan, whose scoring record should outweigh the dissapointment of losing Carney. They have also signed former Hull player Ben Crooks, whose time with Parramatta should serve him well. Rounding off their signings is young and talented full back Ryan Hampshire on loan from Wigan, who will relish the chance to play regularly in Super League. Luke Gale should continue to influence play from the centre of the park and will be vital to any Castleford success.

Catalans

Just like several previous seasons, how well Catalans do will be dependent on their form away from Perpignan. They will no doubt continue their excellent home form, where they only lost two games all season last year. They will look to their star players such as Todd Carney to try and reproduce their home form when they are in England. However, the main struggle for Carney would be to keep him fit after injury limited his game time. The acquisition of seasoned Super League players such as Pat Richards, Richie Myler and Jodie Broughton should help with games away from home. I'd say a season of inconsistency and poor away form is on the cards, leaving them a way off the top four.

Huddersfield

Despite having a strong regular season, Huddersfield once again failed to capitalise during the play offs which is fast becoming a cliche. Brett Ferres is a massive loss for Huddersfield, especially after his good form during the New Zealand series. They have also lost several useful players such as Craig Kopczak and Jodie Broughton. Huddersfield have responded with two signings from the NRL: Ryan Hinchcliffe and Sam Rapira. Larne Patrick also returns after a loan spell at Wigan. This leaves them with an impressive pack once again. However, the success or failure of Huddersfield's season rests with half back Danny Brough. If he plays at his best for most of the season, Huddersfield have the potential to reach the top four.

Hull FC

A season of inconsistency left Hull towards the bottom of the top eight. They have have also lost several key players such as Tom Lineham and Joe Westerman. However, they have recruited strongly during the off season. The biggest signing being the arrival of Frank Pritchard. A veteran of the NRL with international experience with both New Zealand and Samoa should prove to be handy for Hull this year. His signing strengthens the Hull pack considerably. He and new signing Sika Manu should help fill the gap left by Joe Westermans departure. However, the loss of free scoring Tom Lineham will be a blow to the Hull sides attacking options.

Hull KR

Despite missing out on the top eight and falling into the middle eight, Hull KR had a successful 2015. They made a cup final appearance and were unbeaten in the second stage of the competition. The Robins will be aiming to build on that late form to try and reach the top eights. However, they seem to be lacking in the forwards and will be unlikely to challenge the top teams. This is highlighted by the loss of last years acting captain, Tyrone McCarthy, to the NRL. However, the signing of Shaun Lunt on a permanent deal after his successful loan last year will be welcome. They have also signed some good young players such as Thomas Minns and Iain Thornley. If these youngster can settle quickly and make an impression Hull KR may make the top eight. Otherwise, they will be relying on the brilliance of half backs Albert Kelly and Terry Campese.

Leeds

There are two big holes in the shape of Kevin Sinfield and Jamie Peacock for Leeds to fill if they have a chance of being successful this year. Not only did they lose two very talented players, they also lost two leaders in Peacock and Sinfield. Leeds have also lost Paul Aiton to Catalans, an influential player despite his injuries towards the back end of last year. The experience of the likes of Kylie Leuluai will also be missed. A leadership vacuum should be avoided with players like Danny McGuire, Rob Burrow and Jamie Jones-Buchannan still being at the club, but with these players aging their playtime may be limited. The success of this season will most likely rest on the shoulders of Danny McGuire, who has been made captain for this season. The shock signing of Brett Ferres will help fill the void left by Peacock and leaves the Rhino's with an impressive forward pack. Their backs will no doubt be as impressive as ever, with last years Man of Steel Zak Hardaker leading from the rear.

Salford

Salford failed yet again to live up to the owner's, Marwan Koukash, expectations. This led to yet another overhaul of the playing staff. However, with the appointment of former Australia coach, Koukash hopes to add some much needed stability to the team. In a break from previous years, there hasn't been any signing of superstars, just the arrivals of several quality players. While these aren't as exciting as the big names, Koukash will hope they have less volatile personalities than their predecessors. However, they will struggle without the hard runs of Harrison Hansen and the moments of magic from Rangi Chase.

Saints

Saint Helens came close last year, but were eventually knocked out in the semi-final with a defeat to Leeds after a downturn in form towards the back end of the season. Their main signing would have to be Theo Fages from Salford. The young French half back is a great prospect and could challenge the halfback pairing of Travis Burns and Luke Walsh. Saints will be looking for a better year on the injury front, as 2015 saw many injuries for Saints derailing their season. Their signings in the off-season seem to reflect that as they have brought in a lot of depth to their squad including Dominique Peyroux, Jack Owens and Lama Tasi. Saints also have one of the best set of forwards in the competition, boasting Alex Walmsley and Kyle Amor among their ranks, as well as experienced hooker James Roby. A luckier season on the injury front, especially with a fully fit Luke Walsh, should see a serious challenge for silverware this season.

Wakefield

Wakefield had a disastrous season last year, winning only three games over the regular season. The appointment of Brian Smith saw them improve towards the back end of the season and ended up beating Bradford in the Million Pound Game. They have since looked to build on that with an overhaul of the playing squad, bringing in several quality players. One of these is the pacey Ben Jones-Bishop, formerly of Leeds. He will be hoping to be influential in attack, while being steady at the back. Anthony Tupou and Tinirau Arona will look to add strength in attack, while Liam Finn will act as organiser for the team. A high turnover of players may be their downfall but captain Danny Kirmond will look to lead by example.

Warrington

Warrington will be looking to bounce back from a very dissapointing 2015. However, thay have returned this year determined to make amends, starting pre-season training early. They have also signed several players, hoping to freshen up the team. Among them include the experienced Kurt Gidley. A State of Origin representative with over 250 NRL games, he will be looking to use his experience to turn Warrington around. The off-season saw the loss of free-scoring winger, Joel Monaghan, to Castleford. To fill his spot they have brought in the prolific Tom Lineham from Hull. The signing of Gidley and Lineham should add in both attack and defence for the Warrington back line. There may be questions in the half backs after losing both of last years starting halfbacks, Gareth OBrien and Richie Myler. However, Chris Sandow will be looking to step up his performances from the end of last year.

Widnes

Widnes showed a lot of inconsistency and poor defence last year, however showed several passages of great rugby. The mastermind behind this, Kevin Brown, will be hoping for a repeat performance. His expert knowledge of the Widnes home pitch will ensure a solid foundation of home results. Dennis Betts has been quiet in the off season, only recruiting a few new signings, despite losing twelve players. This has led to questions of their depth and could be in trouble should injuries hit. However, the signings they have made are quality, Super League standard players such as Chris Bridge and Setaimata Sa.

Wigan

Wigan came agonisingly close to success last year, being pipped to the post for the League Leaders Shield and the Grand Final by Leeds both times. The standout headline from the off-season was a return English rugby league and to Wigan for the talented Sam Tomkins. However, the full back will miss the start of the season through injury and won't return until March. But when he returns, Wigan fans will expect a lot from him. The return of Tomkins should offset the loss of both Joe Burgess and Matty Bowen to the NRL and retirement respectively. The young English talent at Wigan will only continue to improve, with the likes of George Williams and an in particular John Bateman enjoying experience with England at the end of last season. In the squad are several players with a point to prove such as injury hit Dan Sarginson and Josh Charnley. Leading the forwards will be the reliable Sean O'Loughlin, hoping for a relatively injury free 2016. The mix of both youth and experience should bring rewards for Shaun Wane's side.
